null_A_trajectory_shuffle.description: Shuffle phi_proxy values across tick positions (same value distribution, random order)

null_B_state_hash_shuffle.description: Shuffle state_hash sequence; recompute joint_mi via W=20 sliding entropy; phi = max(0, joint_mi - sub_mi_mean[orig_i])

honest_c3: n=15 ticks gives a permutation pool of 15!=1.3e12 but only ~10 distinct hash values across ticks; effective shuffle entropy is bounded by hash multiplicity, so null-B slope distribution is narrower than a fully random null would yield.

Sub_mi_mean is held in original-position order during Null B (only the joint-hash side is shuffled); this is conservative — a fully-shuffled null would shuffle BOTH and likely yield even smaller slopes, making composite verdict more conservative (against REAL_SIGNAL).

MIP-mean-of-parts surrogate persists from Phase 1/2/3; the shuffle test compares observed-vs-shuffled within the SAME proxy, so MIP slack does not bias the relative comparison but does bound absolute Phi interpretation.

Forward-fill bias and non-stationary cron tick spacing (1s..12h) persist; shuffling redistributes them uniformly across positions but does not eliminate them — both observed and null sit on the same biased substrate.
Single-tail test (slope>=observed) chosen because the alternative hypothesis is RISING; a two-tailed test would double the p-values but not change verdict at the n=1000 / alpha=0.05 thresholds used.
interpretation_one_line: Observed slope +0.1153; null-A p=0.0010 (z=2.45); null-B p=0.9660 (z=-1.44); composite verdict = ARTIFACT_CONFIRMED.
